pharm: Imidazoline sympathomimetic that stimulates alpha-adrenergic receptors, constricting nasal mucosal blood vessels.
quick: Adults/children 7+: 1 spray into each nostril up to 3 times daily
Use only if necessary; prefer short, sparing use
Minimal systemic absorption; use with caution
Duration of use (limit to 3-7 days), rebound congestion
summary: Xylometazoline is a topical imidazoline nasal decongestant that constricts swollen nasal blood vessels to relieve congestion from colds, allergies, and sinusitis. It acts within minutes and lasts several hours. It must be limited to short-term use (typically up to 3-7 days) because prolonged use causes rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa).
indications: Temporary relief of nasal congestion due to the common cold, hay fever, or other upper respiratory allergies
Relief of nasal congestion associated with sinusitis

dosage.c: Nasal congestion (adults and children 7 yr and older)
dosage.d: 1 spray into each nostril up to 3 times daily (0.1% solution)
dosage.n: Do not exceed 3 doses in 24 hours; limit to short-term use

dosage.d: Use the pediatric 0.05% strength per product label and age
dosage.n: Not for use in children under 7 (adult-strength); follow product directions

dosage.d: Limit continuous use to no more than 3-7 days

admin: Blow the nose gently before use
Spray into each nostril while breathing in gently; keep the head upright
Wipe the nozzle clean after use; do not share the device to avoid spreading infection
Do not use for more than 3-7 days continuously
Do not exceed the recommended frequency
moa: Xylometazoline is a sympathomimetic imidazoline that directly stimulates alpha-adrenergic receptors on nasal mucosal arterioles, causing vasoconstriction. This reduces blood flow and mucosal swelling, decongesting the nasal passages and improving airflow.

absolute: After transsphenoidal hypophysectomy or surgery exposing the dura mater (per some labels)
monitor: Duration of use to prevent rebound congestion

preg: Use only if clearly necessary and for the shortest time; prefer sparing use because systemic vasoconstrictors may theoretically affect placental flow with excessive use.
lact: Systemic absorption is minimal with proper intranasal use; use with caution and avoid excessive or prolonged use while breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment; systemic absorption is minimal with topical use.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment; systemic absorption is minimal with topical use.

major: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (current or within 14 days): risk of hypertensive crisis
interactions.diagnostics: No significant laboratory test interference expected with topical use.

serious: Rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa) with prolonged use
Systemic effects with overuse (hypertension, palpitations, headache)
emergency: CNS depression/coma in young children after accidental ingestion or overdose

counsel: Do not use for more than 3-7 days; longer use can worsen congestion
Do not exceed the recommended number of sprays per day
Mild stinging or dryness in the nose can occur
Do not share the spray device with others
Keep out of reach of children; accidental swallowing can be dangerous, especially for young children
pk: Store at room temperature; keep the container tightly closed
pearls: Fast local relief but strictly short-term to avoid rebound congestion
Rhinitis medicamentosa develops with continuous use beyond about a week
Minimal systemic absorption when used correctly, but overuse can cause cardiovascular effects
Accidental ingestion in young children can cause serious CNS and cardiovascular depression
missed: Used as needed for symptom relief, so there is no scheduled missed dose. Take the next dose when needed, without exceeding the daily limit.
overdose: Overdose or accidental ingestion (especially in children) can cause sedation, bradycardia, hypotension or hypertension, hypothermia, and respiratory depression. Provide supportive care with airway support and monitoring; there is no specific antidote.
